# `silk/system/glob_scan`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Find the files and directories that a glob pattern matches, by walking directories through
the `FileSystem` effect.

## When to use
Use [`scan`](#scan) to collect every match of a pattern such as `src/**/*.silk`, or a [`Walker`](#Walker) to
take matches one at a time. To test paths you already have, use `silk.text.glob` directly.

## Details
A scan reads only the directories its pattern can reach. A literal segment is looked up
directly, a wildcard segment lists one directory, and `**` descends into every directory
below. Results are relative to [`ScanOptions.base`](#ScanOptions.base), joined with `/`, with `.` and `..`
segments of the pattern resolved, and each one is reported once. A pattern that starts with
`/` is scanned from the provider's root and reports absolute paths. The order of results is
unspecified.

Names are host bytes and are reported as they are, also when they are not UTF-8.

A literal segment follows a symbolic link, so `docs/*.md` works when `docs` is a link to a
directory. A link that a wildcard matched is never entered, which also keeps a scan from
looping through a cycle of links; it is reported only when [`ScanOptions.onlyFiles`](#ScanOptions.onlyFiles) is
false.

Every read goes through the `FileSystem` effect, so a scan sees exactly what the provider
shows, and a provider in memory or one that records reads works the same way.

## Errors
- `FileError` if the starting directory is missing or is not a directory, or if a directory
  cannot be read for a reason other than its having gone away.
- `OutOfMemoryError` from every operation that returns owned paths.

## Examples
### Find the Silk sources of a project
```silk
import silk.system.glob_scan { ScanOptions, scan }
import silk.system.filesystem { FileError, FileSystem, Path }
import silk.system.filesystem_native { OsFileSystem }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

effect fn program() -> i32 ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut FileSystem | &mut Allocator {
  let root = run Path.root()
  let scratch = run FileSystem.temporaryDirectory(&root, "silk-glob-")
  run FileSystem.writeFileWithParents(&run Path.join(&scratch.path, "src/main.silk"), b"")
  run FileSystem.writeFileWithParents(&run Path.join(&scratch.path, "src/net/http.silk"), b"")
  run FileSystem.writeFileWithParents(&run Path.join(&scratch.path, "README.md"), b"")
  let options = run ScanOptions.make(&scratch.path)
  let found = run scan("src/**/*.silk", move options)
  let count = List<Bytes>.length(&found)
  drop found
  run FileSystem.release(move scratch)
  if count != 2 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed<E>(error: E) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

effect fn withFiles() -> i32 ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut files = run OsFileSystem.make("/tmp")
  return run program() |> Effect.provideMut<FileSystem>(&mut files)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(withFiles(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="Walker.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(written: string, options: ScanOptions) -> Walker
    ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut FileSystem | &mut Allocator
```

Starts a scan for the pattern `written` below `options.base`, or below the provider's root
when `written` starts with `/`.

#### Details

The pattern is split at `/` into segments, and each directory is read only when a segment
can match below it: `src/*.silk` lists `src` and nothing else. Braces and groups work within
one segment; an alternative that contains `/`, such as `{a/b,c}`, is not scanned. A pattern
that ends with `/` reports directories only, and so reports nothing while `onlyFiles` is
set. An empty pattern reports nothing.

#### Errors

- `FileError` if the starting directory does not exist or is not a directory.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the walker.

<a id="scan"></a>

## `scan`

```silk
pub effect fn scan(pattern: string, options: ScanOptions) -> List<Bytes>
  ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut FileSystem | &mut Allocator
```

Returns every path that `pattern` matches below `options.base`, in unspecified order.

### Details

It is [`Walker.make`](#Walker.impl.make) followed by [`Walker.collect`](#Walker.impl.collect); the walker's rules apply.

### Errors

- The errors of [`Walker.make`](#Walker.impl.make) and [`Walker.next`](#Walker.impl.next).
